analysis: Examined DistributedInstalledPairServingGrant.swift. Head 1-503 covers chip classing, mode families, grant/decision construction and record contradiction; none of it is changed. Chip class comes from the local sysctl brand string (head 45-55), and the bench override is debug-only. Inconsistent or unclassed records are ignored (head 434-435). A pass contradicted by a same-shape divergence grants nothing (head 457-465). Changed lines are limited to publicTrafficLine (base 661-674, head 661-678) and the tensorAssistantNotOffered doc/text (base 788-792, head ~794-795). The patch makes three changes. The default publicModels source changes from ClusterPublicModels.declared to ClusterPublicModels.current. The "not offered for public traffic" line is now suppressed when the owner declared a tensor assistant public for the installed artifact (ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant). A nil artifactSHA256 keeps the old behavior. This function only produces display text for plans and onboarding. Visible code shows no public-traffic admission decision made from it. Public serving still requires the coordinator's cluster approval and parity qualification (base 826, head 172-174). Owner declaration therefore does not by itself grant public traffic in visible code. No regression identified. Integration questions: (1) Do ClusterPublicModels.current/tensorAssistant and ClusterConfiguration.validate actually gate offering a tensor-assistant placement to the coordinator? Is the coordinator's parity qualification bound to the assistant (MTP) configuration, so an owner-declared assistant cannot be publicly served without qualification? This relates to T-007/T-056 and output integrity. (2) Could the new text overclaim "qualified for public traffic" for an assistant setup that no cross-cable record covers? This is documentation/UX only unless the routing path consumes it. The head-side changed lines 664-678 were not in the supplied units, and the ClusterPublicModels sources were not supplied.
